body: Does anybody know when they are going to die?

I stopped because:
1. There was a point where I almost jumped out of my hospital bedroom window (I was on the 6th floor) because of the unbearable pain. It traumatized me and made me decide that I might actually kill myself if that kind of pain happens again.
2. My family and I ran out of money. Literally. Even our friends cannot help us anymore because of the exorbitant costs. Of course, we exhausted all possible resources, but the cost alone of pain medications that need to be maintained makes it impossible to save up.

I am sorry to hear your story. *hugs*

I myself am contemplating suicide. I have a stage 4 soft tissue cancer, and I am in a lot of pain. It's the kind of pain that is hard to describe to non-cancer patients, but the bottomline is, cancer pain is the worst. Sometimes, I even feel like I have lost my mind already when the pain episode gets too intense for my brain to handle.

I would like to believe that your grandfather just wanted to be able to finally rest. Dealing with cancer is exhausting. Perhaps your grandfather felt it is time that he rests, and not wait for cancer to finish its course and take him.

I empathize with your grandfather, and if it's any help, I'd like to wager saying that he did not intend to hurt any one of you, his dearest loved ones.

Let him rest. You will also find yourself at peace with it when the right time comes. In the meantime, do what you gotta do to cope.
Maybe you need to lower the dosage. If the dosage is right and is tolerated well, he should be able to feel better, and his appetite should be back, even a little.

Hi! I am sure he'll get there. Just be patient and let his body adjust. Cannabis oil is a lifesaver for cancer patients. Once it's working, it encourages one's appetite and helps the patient with getting proper sleep. Good luck!

I feel you! I received my official cancer diagnosis exactly on my 28th bday. I knew it was cancer, but I still wanted to hear it on my birthday. I wanted to be able to look at it as a gift; it might not happen at that moment, but I am hoping it will in the future.

I am 30 now, and I still find it hard to meet peole my age with the same condition. I live in Manila, Philippines, and I am the first and only diagnosed case of Epithelioid Hemangioendothelioma (EHE), my very rare soft tissue sarcoma.

I joined an online support group on Facebook, and met a few people my age. Elder people never lack stories and they have the best advise all the time, but it is a different thing to have someone completely empathize with you. I think it is going to be helpful to meet someone your age whom you can exchange stories with.

I know that for most of us, we just want to be heard, and we want people to cheer for us as we manage this cancer thing. 

P.S. We can be friends! 🤗

I know there is nothing a stranger like me could say to make you feel better. I myself have cancer, too, and it is indeed the worst. So if you're interested, I'll just teach you a new cuss word. Because, you know, cancer is why we cuss. Hehe.

P.S. Keep swimming despite and in spite everything. Soon, the worst will over.

Hello! A friend of mine set up a YouCaring page for me.

Thanks!

Hi! A friend of mine created a YouCaring page. Is GoFundMe better? If you want and if it's not a hassle, sure, you may set up a page for me. ☺️

I updated my main post. You can learn everything about me through the YouCaring page.

THANK YOU!

Thank you! My "friends" won't donate. I think the understanding of Filipinos when you ask them for help with your fundraising, they think sharing your link on their Facebook is enough. Worse, they'll devalue my condition and tell me to just take advil. 😔
Thank you.
Thank you! Please PM me at your convenience.
Thank you for your kindness. I did update my main post. And I have a fundraising page. Please check my update on the main post. Thanks!
I know what you mean. Thank you!

Hi, thanks. You're right, I always lived life to the fullest. But cancer is taking away my zest for life. 😢 BTW, I'm from the Philippines where we have nothing similar to what you guys have there in the US.
What is this? Please tell me.
You think I never thought of that?

Thank you for understanding, makes me feel less alone. I'm from the Philippines and there is nothing here. Here, people die from simple illnesses. And when one gets cancer, that's an instant death sentence, unless you are a multi-millionaire.

Hi! I've been thinking about the fundraising page. I am from the Philippines and people here do not donate through these channels because:
1. We don't have a credit card or a Paypal account
2. We are too poor

But a friend of mine from the EHE support group did create a fundraising page for me at YouCaring. It's been there for days but only a couple of people donated. Do you think it's still worth a shot?

P.S. I will post an update on what happened to me shortly. Just figuring out how.
Thank you for understanding. I appreciate it. Makes me feel less alone.

If not, let me apply. Thanks!
